ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 4 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction, making it the single strongest consensus idea this morning. The stock trades at ~25x forward earnings — a multi-year low and near market parity with the S&P 500 — despite ~95% projected YoY revenue growth and $600B+ in committed hyperscaler capex from Alphabet ($195-205B) and Amazon ($220B) that screens argue is still unpriced. With Q2 FY2027 earnings confirmed for August 26 after close, the company's own guidance of $91B in Q2 revenue sits below the current analyst consensus of $92-94B, suggesting a beat-and-raise setup. A defined-risk call spread (Aug29 or Sep expiry) is the preferred structure over outright stock given post-earnings binary vol risk.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings report — August 26, 2026 after market close (6 days away)
ideas.edge: 68-analyst consensus price target of $303.09 vs ~$225 current = ~35% implied upside gap; forward P/E ~25x vs. historical pre-earnings norm of 35-40x implies 20%+ re-rating to 30x alone; revenue estimates revised up 6.67% in past 3 months
ideas.bull_case: A beat-and-raise on Aug 26 against a depressed ~25x fwd PE multiple re-rates the stock toward its historical 35-40x range, closing a large portion of the 35% gap to the $303 consensus target; hyperscaler capex tailwinds provide multi-quarter demand visibility.
ideas.bear_case: Post-earnings vol has been punishing in prior NVDA cycles regardless of print quality; a hawkish FOMC surprise today or Jackson Hole could compress the entire tech multiple before the Aug 26 event, capping any re-rating.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (Nasdaq ADR)
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 4 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction. The stock is trading ~12% below its July 10 Nasdaq debut price and ~55-60% below Bank of America's $250 price target (initiated August 20) despite being structurally locked in as NVIDIA's primary HBM co-developer within a $500B+ AI infrastructure partnership. SK Hynix announced a $29B (40 trillion won) share buyback on August 19 representing >50% of FCF committed to shareholder returns through 2025-2027, providing a hard floor catalyst. Operating margin hit 76% last quarter with net income up 108% YoY — a fundamental profile that screens argue is deeply mispriced at current levels near $155-165.
ideas.catalyst: BofA $250 Buy rating initiated August 20, 2026 + $29B buyback announced August 19, 2026; Q3 earnings with full shareholder return details forthcoming
ideas.edge: BofA $250 price target vs. ~$155-165 current price = ~55-60% implied upside; $29B buyback = >50% of FCF 2025-2027 committed to shareholder returns; stock trades ~12% below Nasdaq debut price despite strengthening fundamentals (net income +108% YoY, 76% operating margin)
ideas.bull_case: The combination of a massive buyback floor, a fresh institutional Buy rating with a $250 target, and structural lock-in as Nvidia's sole HBM co-developer positions SKHY for a significant re-rating as AI infrastructure spending continues to accelerate.
ideas.bear_case: As a newly listed ADR, SKHY carries liquidity and FX risk; any deterioration in the broader AI trade or a delay in the Nvidia HBM supply ramp could pressure the stock further below its already-disappointing debut price.

ideas.thesis: XLE appeared in 2 of 4 overnight screens as a geopolitical hedge. ideas.catalyst: Imminent diplomatic deadline or military headline on Iran Strait of Hormuz standoff following ceasefire expiry August 18, 2026
ideas.edge: Oil at ~$85/barrel with geopolitical risk premium building; Brent analyst upside scenario to $138 if Strait of Hormuz closes further; XLE up ~21% YTD with energy sector projecting 20%+ earnings growth Q3-Q4 2026 — one of only 8 S&P sectors at that threshold

ideas.bear_case: Geopolitical risk premiums can unwind rapidly on diplomatic breakthroughs; a surprise de-escalation or OPEC supply response could reverse oil's recent run and compress XLE quickly, particularly if rising rates simultaneously pressure equity multiples.
